stemMd: A device uses 600 W for 5 minutes. How much electrical energy does it consume?
explanationMd: Power is energy per second. Five minutes is 300 seconds, so energy equals 600 × 300 = 180,000 J. The time unit must match the watt’s joules-per-second definition.

distractorRationale.d: This multiplies watts by minutes without converting minutes to seconds.
distractorRationale.b: This divides power by time rather than multiplying.
distractorRationale.a: This uses an incorrect power-time product.
distractorRationale.e: This would be the energy used in one second only.
